findings.evidence: `grep -n 'FG' TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/LocalizationTopology.lean` returns nothing. `PairOfDefinition.fg_idealOfDefinition : idealOfDefinition.FG` (Huber/Basic.lean:92) supplies the hypothesis and `Ideal.FG.map {I : Ideal R} (h : I.FG) (f : R →+* S) : (I.map f).FG` (mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Ideal.lean:27) the step; `locIdeal_def` (line 217) is `Ideal.map (algebraMapD P T s) P.idealOfDefinition`.
findings.fix: Add `theorem fg_locIdeal (P : PairOfDefinition A) (T : Finset A) (s : A) : (locIdeal P T s).FG := locIdeal_def P T s ▸ P.fg_idealOfDefinition.map (algebraMapD P T s)`, and reduce the docstring's remaining-conditions note to the `J`-adic identification alone.
findings.issue: `locIdeal` has no finite-generation lemma, yet the module docstring (lines 49-51) lists `J` being finitely generated alongside the genuinely deferred `J`-adic identification as what is still missing for `(D, J)` to be a `PairOfDefinition`. It is a one-liner from existing API, so a consumer assembling the pair must re-derive it and the doc misrepresents it as open work.

summary: The surface is minimal, bodies stay hidden behind `(rfl)`-restatements, and the simp set on `divByS` is confluent — I verified Mathlib's `IsLocalization.Away.mul_invSelf` is `@[simp]` (mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/Away/Basic.lean:61), so the mirror lemmas the `reuse` lane wants deleted are what keeps `invSelf s * algebraMap A S s` reaching `1`; my earlier requirement for them stands. Two gaps remain: `locIdeal` lacks the finite-generation lemma its own docstring names as an open condition, and the module doc advertises a surface that does not match the declarations.
